reader.notes: AbbrevCarry threads subject and operator in source order through BindFlatSequence; a parenthesized or non-relation condition resets it. The 85 arm of the logical NOT (BindNegatedAbbreviatedRelation without Has(2002)) is the 1985 reading and differs from the latest by design. All printed examples and the edge cases computed the expected truth values.

refuter.evidence: The 1985 format is 'relation-condition {AND|OR} [NOT] [relational-operator] object', and the 1985 relational operators include 'IS [NOT] LESS THAN / IS [NOT] <' with IS optional (§1985:VI.6.3.1.1 format, line 12029, IS not underlined; cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.6.3.1.1  (6.3.1.1 Relation Condition)  'Greater than or not greater than'; table 1 sentence: OK  §1985:VI.6.3.2.3  'the pair NOT NOT is not permissible'). So 'A > 1 AND NOT NOT < 5' is [NOT]=NOT, relational-operator='NOT <', object=5. By GRL2.1 the word after the first NOT is NOT, not one of GREATER > LESS < EQUAL =, so by GRL2.2 that NOT is logical: ((A > 1) AND (NOT (A NOT < 5))), which complies with table 1 (NOT followed by a simple-condition; the second NOT is inside the relational operator, not a logical element). Probes: ab1.cob at --std 85: 'IF A > 1 AND NOT NOT < 5' and 'IF A > 1 AND NOT NOT < 2' -> error COBOL0001: cannot parse construct near 'NOT' (both lines). ab6.cob at --std 85, the SAME form with the optional IS written: 'IF A > 1 AND NOT IS NOT < 5' compiles and prints N6 T (correct), and the unabbreviated 'NOT A NOT < 5' and 'A > 1 AND NOT A NOT < 5' print U1 T / U2 T. So the refusal depends only on whether optional IS is written. Cause: CobolParserCoreBase.cs#logicalNotBeforeRelationalOperator excludes NOT as LA(2) ('and NOT, which no reading lets follow NOT', grammar comment at CobolExpressions.g4#negatedAbbreviatedRelation), and comparisonOperator has no 'NOT NOT <' alternative. ab1b.cob at --std 2023: same COBOL0001 (edition-blind predicate). Other probes held: ab2 'OR NOT GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO 2' and ab3 'OR NOT LESS OR EQUAL 2' refused (NOT joins GREATER/LESS by GRL2.1 and NOT GREATER THAN OR EQUAL is no 1985 operator); ab4 '<>' -> COBOL0900; ab5 'OR IS 3' refused; N3 'OR NOT IS > 4' T, N4 'OR IS NOT > 2' F, N5 'OR GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO 3' T, all right for A=3. cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.6.3.3 SR2 (the format is in SR2's text); OK  §1985:VI.6.3.3 GRL2.1  'If the word immediately following NOT is GREATER'; OK  §1985:VI.6.3.3 GRL2.2  'The NOT is interpreted as a logical operator'; OK  §1985:III  'IS [NOT] LESS THAN'. Reading that would save the verdict: Table 1's sentence 'the pair NOT NOT is not permissible' read lexically; rejected because table 1 ranges over logical elements and the compiler itself accepts the identical semantics when IS is written.
